q: Net National Product (NNP) is obtained by subtracting what from Gross National Product?
x: NNP = GNP minus depreciation, the wear and tear of capital goods during the year. Subtracting net indirect taxes from NNP at market prices gives national income, or NNP at factor cost.
e: Gross becomes Net when you take out depreciation.

q: A situation of rising prices together with stagnant output and high unemployment is called what?
x: Stagflation combines stagnation with inflation — prices keep rising even though growth has stalled and unemployment is high.
e: Stagnation + inflation = stagflation.

q: The Lorenz curve is used to show what?
x: The Lorenz curve plots the share of income against the share of population. The further it bends away from the line of equality, the greater the inequality; the Gini coefficient measures that gap.
e: Lorenz curve draws inequality; the Gini coefficient puts a number on it.

q: Engel's law relates a rise in income to a fall in which share of spending?
x: Engel's law states that as a family's income rises, the proportion of income spent on food falls, even though the amount spent may rise.
e: Richer households still buy food — it just takes up a smaller slice of the budget.

q: Goods whose demand falls as consumer income rises are called what?
x: An inferior good is one people buy less of as they grow richer, because they switch to a better substitute — coarse grain giving way to finer grain, for example.
e: Inferior good: more income, less demand.

q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in which year?
x: The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
e: Act 1934, started 1935, nationalised 1949.

q: The repo rate is the rate at which what happens?
o: Commercial banks lend to their best customers
Banks lend to one another overnight
The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The RBI borrows from commercial banks
x: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities. The rate at which the RBI borrows from banks is the reverse repo rate.
e: Repo: RBI lends. Reverse repo: RBI borrows.

q: The portion of a bank's deposits that it must keep as cash with the RBI is called what?
x: The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of net demand and time liabilities a bank must hold in cash with the RBI. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio is the share it must keep in its own safe assets such as government securities and gold.
e: CRR sits with the RBI as cash; SLR stays with the bank as safe assets.

q: How many commercial banks were nationalised in India in the first round of 1969?
x: Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised in July 1969; six more followed in April 1980.
e: 14 in 1969, 6 in 1980 — twenty banks in all.

q: Which institution is the apex bank for agriculture and rural development in India?
x: NABARD, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, was set up in 1982 as the apex body for rural credit and development finance.
e: NABARD rural, SIDBI small industry, EXIM foreign trade.

q: Gresham's law in economics states that what happens?
o: Bad money drives out good money
x: Gresham's law says that when two kinds of money of the same legal value circulate together, people spend the poorer one and hoard the better one, so bad money drives good money out of circulation.
e: People keep the good coin and pass on the worn one.

q: The First Five Year Plan of India gave the highest priority to which sector?
x: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and concentrated on agriculture, irrigation and power after the disruption of Partition. It met its targets.
e: First Plan farms (Harrod-Domar); Second Plan factories (Mahalanobis).

q: The Second Five Year Plan of India was based on the model developed by whom?
x: The Second Plan (1956-61) followed P. C. Mahalanobis's model, which put heavy and basic industry at the centre of growth. Steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur came from it.
e: Mahalanobis = heavy industry = the Second Plan.

q: NITI Aayog replaced which body on 1 January 2015?
x: NITI Aayog — the National Institution for Transforming India — replaced the Planning Commission, which had been set up in 1950. The Prime Minister chairs it.
e: Planning Commission 1950 to 2014; NITI Aayog from 1 January 2015.

q: Under which Article does the President cause the annual financial statement, or Union Budget, to be laid before Parliament?
x: Article 112 requires the annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure to be laid before both Houses for every financial year. The Constitution never uses the word 'Budget'.
e: 112 Budget, 110 Money Bill, 266 Consolidated Fund, 280 Finance Commission.

q: The Goods and Services Tax came into force in India on which date?
x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2016, replacing a long list of central and state indirect taxes.
e: 101st Amendment (2016) → GST from 1 July 2017.

q: MGNREGA guarantees how many days of wage employment in a financial year to a rural household?
x: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, guarantees at least 100 days of unskilled manual work in a financial year to every rural household whose adults volunteer for it.
e: 100 days, rural household, unskilled manual work, on demand.

q: The Green Revolution in India is particularly associated with which crop?
x: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s rested on high-yielding dwarf varieties of wheat, chiefly in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. M. S. Swaminathan led the Indian effort and Norman Borlaug bred the varieties.
e: Swaminathan in India, Borlaug abroad, wheat in Punjab.

q: How many base units are there in the International System of Units (SI)?
x: The SI has seven base units: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. All other units are derived from these.
e: Seven base units — length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount, light.

q: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of what?
x: Newton's first law says a body stays at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless an external force acts on it. That tendency to resist a change of state is inertia.
e: First law inertia, second law F = ma, third law action and reaction.

q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
x: Pressure is force per unit area, so its SI unit is the pascal, equal to one newton per square metre.
e: Force newton, pressure pascal, work joule, power watt.

q: The working of a hydraulic brake is based on which principle?
x: Pascal's law says pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in every direction. Hydraulic brakes and hydraulic lifts both use it.
e: Pascal's law: a small push on a small piston becomes a big push on a big one.

q: Sound cannot travel through which of the following?
x: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to carry it. A vacuum has no particles to vibrate, so sound cannot pass through it. Sound travels fastest in solids.
e: No medium, no sound — which is why space is silent.

q: Sound waves of frequency above 20,000 hertz are called what?
x: The human ear hears roughly 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Above that range the waves are ultrasonic; below it they are infrasonic. 'Supersonic' describes speed, not frequency.
e: Ultrasound is used in medical scans and in cleaning; bats use it to navigate.

q: Heat transfer by the actual movement of heated particles of a fluid is called what?
x: In convection, heated fluid becomes less dense, rises and carries heat with it, while cooler fluid sinks to take its place. Land and sea breezes work this way.
e: Conduction through solids, convection in fluids, radiation needs no medium.

q: The blue colour of the clear sky is caused by which phenomenon?
x: Air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths much more strongly than longer ones, so blue light is spread across the sky. The same effect makes the setting Sun look red.
e: Blue scatters most, red scatters least — that is why sunsets are red.

q: A mirage seen on a hot road is caused by which phenomenon?
x: Hot air near the road is less dense than the air above it. Light from the sky bends gradually and is then totally internally reflected, so the road appears to carry a pool of water.
e: Mirage = refraction through layers of air ending in total internal reflection.

q: Short-sightedness, or myopia, is corrected using which type of lens?
x: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina, so a diverging — concave — lens is used to push it back. Long-sightedness is corrected with a convex lens.
e: Myopia concave, hypermetropia convex, astigmatism cylindrical.

q: According to Ohm's law, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to what, at constant temperature?
x: Ohm's law states V = IR: at constant temperature the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across its ends.
e: V = IR — voltage up, current up; resistance up, current down.

q: Domestic electrical appliances are connected in which arrangement?
x: House wiring uses parallel connections so each appliance gets the full supply voltage and can be switched on or off without affecting the others.
e: Parallel at home: one bulb failing does not stop the rest.

q: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of what?
x: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus, and it fixes the identity of the element. Protons plus neutrons give the mass number.
e: Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons.

q: Who discovered the nucleus of the atom through the gold foil experiment?
x: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment on thin gold foil in 1911 showed that an atom's positive charge and nearly all its mass sit in a tiny central nucleus.
e: Thomson found the electron, Rutherford the nucleus, Chadwick the neutron.

q: The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of what?
x: Moseley's work showed that properties repeat according to atomic number, not atomic mass as Mendeleev had assumed. That change resolved the anomalies in Mendeleev's table.
e: Mendeleev used atomic mass; Moseley corrected it to atomic number.

q: Which is the chemical symbol for potassium?
x: Potassium's symbol K comes from its Latin name kalium. P is phosphorus, Pt is platinum and Po is polonium.
e: Latin-based symbols: K kalium, Na natrium, Fe ferrum, Au aurum, Ag argentum, Pb plumbum.

q: Diamond and graphite are both forms of which element?
x: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon. In diamond each carbon is bonded to four others, which makes it the hardest natural substance; graphite's layered structure makes it soft and able to conduct electricity.
e: Same element, different arrangement — hardest substance and pencil lead both pure carbon.

q: What is the pH value of a neutral solution at 25 degrees Celsius?
x: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14; 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic. Pure water at 25 degrees Celsius has a pH of 7.
e: Below 7 sour, 7 neutral, above 7 bitter and slippery.

q: The rusting of iron is an example of which type of reaction?
x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide, formed when iron is oxidised in the presence of both oxygen and moisture. Coating the iron with zinc — galvanisation — prevents it.
e: Rusting needs air and water together; remove either and iron does not rust.

q: The chemical name of baking soda is what?
x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na2CO3.10H2O.
e: Baking soda bicarbonate; washing soda carbonate.

q: The acid present in a lemon is which one?
x: Lemons and other citrus fruits contain citric acid. Vinegar has acetic acid, curd has lactic acid and tomatoes contain oxalic acid.
e: Lemon citric, vinegar acetic, curd lactic, ant sting formic, tamarind tartaric.

q: Brass is an alloy of copper and which other metal?
x: Brass is copper with zinc; bronze is copper with tin. Steel is iron with carbon, and stainless steel adds chromium and nickel.
e: Brass has zinc, bronze has tin — both start with copper.

q: Dry ice is the solid form of which substance?
x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide. It sublimes straight from solid to gas without melting, which is why it leaves no liquid behind.
e: Dry ice is 'dry' because it never turns into a liquid.

q: The main constituent of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is which gas?
x: CNG is mostly methane. LPG, the cooking gas in cylinders, is mainly a mixture of butane and propane.
e: CNG methane for vehicles; LPG butane and propane for the kitchen.
